Magnetic Field. A vector field that exerts a force on moving electric charges and magnetic dipoles, analogous to how an electric field acts on static charges. Represented by magnetic field lines emanating from poles, magnetic fields are generated by moving charges, permanent magnets, and quantum spin. Magnetism is intertwined with electricity through electromagnetism, described by Maxwell's equations, and is fundamental to countless technologies from motors to MRI scanners.

Magnetic fields are measured in Tesla, or T, in SI units. Earth's magnetic field is approximately twenty-five to sixty-five microtesla depending on location. The Lorentz force on a charged particle moving through a magnetic field is F equals q times v cross B, perpendicular to both velocity and field. This is the basis of cyclotron motion and particle accelerators.

Bar magnets have north and south poles. Opposite poles attract, and like poles repel. Unlike electric charges, isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist, though they are theoretically predicted. Moving electric charges create magnetic fields. A current-carrying wire generates a circular magnetic field around itself. The right-hand rule governs direction.

Electromagnets use electric current through coils to create strong magnetic fields. By varying current, they can be switched on and off, enabling electromagnetic relays and actuators. Earth's magnetic field is likely generated by convection currents in the liquid outer core. It protects the planet from solar wind and radiation. Its poles precess slowly over millennia.

Quantum mechanically, electrons possess intrinsic magnetic moment called spin. Aligned spins in atoms or materials create permanent magnetism as in ferromagnets. The Stern-Gerlach experiment revealed spin by splitting a beam of silver atoms in an inhomogeneous magnetic field, demonstrating that spin is quantized.

Electromagnetism is the unified framework combining electricity and magnetism through Maxwell's equations. The Lorentz force is the force exerted by a magnetic field on moving charges. An inductor is a component that stores energy by generating a magnetic field. Spin is the intrinsic quantum angular momentum giving particles an inherent magnetic moment. The Stern-Gerlach experiment revealed spin's quantization through magnetic field deflection.
